title: Foreign Interference Commission + Bill C-70 Registry

key_findings: Some parliamentarians showed poor judgment and troubling conduct with foreign powers
Conduct did not amount to treason — situation not as extreme as NSICOP report suggested
NSICOP report made strongly worded allegations against individual parliamentarians based on intelligence
Intelligence is not evidence — cannot be considered conclusive
recommendations_key: Hotline for Canadians to report foreign interference
Ban foreigners (non-PR) from voting in nomination/leadership contests
All federal party leaders should obtain top-secret security clearance
About half can be implemented before next election

poilievre_clearance.finding: Poilievre is the ONLY federal party leader who refused top-secret security clearance
poilievre_clearance.context: He has 12 documented connections in the Israel influence network and led CPC bloc NAY on Gaza ceasefire

bill_c70.purpose: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act — creates registry
bill_c70.commissioner: Former BC Chief Electoral Officer (2018-2025) nominated
bill_c70.scope: All levels of government including municipalities and Indigenous processes
bill_c70.cija_implication: Once operational, CIJA activities may require registration as foreign influence — this is the registry that Senator Woo opposed
bill_c70.woo_connection: Woo argued registry would lead to anti-Asian exclusion, met UFWD-linked leaders 3 days before challenging the Commission

fitaa_status.act: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act (FITAA)
fitaa_status.gap: FITAA passed but registry NOT YET active. No commissioner appointed. No regulations written. Zero foreign agents registered. CIJA, Confucius Institutes, and other foreign influence operations continue WITHOUT disclosure requirements.
fitaa_status.relevance_to_504: Bae Confucius Institute connection would require disclosure under FITAA — but FITAA is not active, so no mechanism to force disclosure exists.
fitaa_status.days_since_royal_assent: Day 658+ since Royal Assent with no operational registry

hogue_government_response.criticism: Government acted too slowly and was insufficiently transparent
hogue_government_response.one_year_report: Commission required one-year progress report to Parliament
hogue_government_response.implementation_update_2026: No government implementation update has surfaced as of April 2026

chinese_police_stations.montreal_investigation: RCMP closed Montreal-area investigation September 2025 WITHOUT charges
chinese_police_stations.defamation_lawsuit: Targeted community organizations filed $4.9M defamation lawsuit against RCMP
chinese_police_stations.funding_loss: Organizations lost approximately 70% of funding ($700-800K/year) due to public allegations
chinese_police_stations.other_stations: Whether stations continue to operate elsewhere remains unconfirmed by RCMP
